title: W15/VC-5: Inspector overview nested tree from observed grouping/ownership edges plus bounded graph fan-out collapse
description:
Gap: layoutInspector (src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts) prints the overview as a flat list under the heading "Observed tree · display grouping only"; reduceInspectorKey toggles state.collapsed on Enter but no row is ever hidden; the graph view already pages relations (bounded 100 via relationsFor) but only prints two and a generic '... additional observed relations (bounded)' line. The spec requires a compact nested tree, fan-out collapsing and explicit cycle references, all computed from the viewport window and the topology-revision relation cache, never from event history.

Scope (atomic, hot-file free): inside src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts only, derive a per-visible-row depth from incoming 'grouping'/'ownership' relations (cap 8, cycle -> '[ref]' line), indent rows, hide descendants of collapsed keys within the fetched window page and show '... N collapsed (observed grouping)', mark rows with no observed parent explicitly, and make the graph view's fan-out line carry a real bounded count with '(partial)' when the relation page is full. Dependency/causation/hypothesis edges must never produce nesting. Works today with fixture relations; the sibling VC-4 bead (Furnace Run->Attempt ownership edges) is the first real producer and is not a dependency.

Files: src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts; test/workbench-inspector.test.ts. Specs: docs/workbench/10 (Four views; Navigation; Rendering pipeline; Failure and deception defenses), docs/workbench/09 (Relationships are typed and provenanced), docs/workbench/02 WB-027/WB-029/WB-037.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first tests added to test/workbench-inspector.test.ts (never delete or weaken the existing five cases) and minimal implementation confined to src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts. No new ObservationProjection API: use only window(), indexOf(), relations() and relationRevision(). Hot files (src/ui/workflow-card.ts, src/index.ts, ...) untouched; src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts should not need changes.

B1. Overview nesting: a fixture with 'grouping' relations three levels deep (provenance.source 'fixture-producer') plus one 'ownership' edge (provenance.source equal to from.provider and a nativeConfirmationRef, as relate() requires) renders each visible row indented 2 columns per depth with ASCII '|-' / Unicode glyph prefixes; depth is derived ONLY from incoming 'grouping' or 'ownership' relations, computed per visible row through the existing relationsFor cache keyed by relationRevision(), and capped at 8.
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" Overview: "compact nested tree". Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "grouping only (phase, display scope)".

B2. Dependency edges never nest: a dependency-only fixture renders every row at depth 0; a row with no incoming grouping/ownership edge shows an explicit 'no observed parent' marker rather than being presented as a root of anything.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Missing edges do not imply independence." Quote: docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-037: "Source-defined edges, observed edges and inferred links are distinguishable."

B3. Cycles: a grouping cycle A->B->A terminates at the first repeated key, renders the repeat as a '[ref ...]' reference line, and layoutInspector returns within the row budget (no infinite loop, lines.length <= rows).
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" Graph: "Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as \"references\" rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan."

B4. Collapse works: after Enter on a parent row (existing collapsed state), rows in the current viewport window whose ancestor chain includes that key are hidden and the parent row shows '... N collapsed (observed grouping)' where N counts only members of the fetched window page, never a full-projection scan; a second Enter restores them.
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Navigation": "Enter expands" and section "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally."

B5. Graph fan-out: a node with more than two outgoing relations prints the first two plus '... +N more (fan-out collapsed; bounded)' with N computed from the bounded relations() page and suffixed '(partial)' when that page is full (100).
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" Graph: "fan-out collapsing" and "Re-layout only changed neighborhood or viewport, not the complete graph for every event."

B6. Bounds preserved under scale: after 100,000 ingest() updates, layoutInspector still issues window() calls with limit <= 32 (existing spy assertion), calls relations() at most twice per visible row per relationRevision (spy count), and for widths 32/79/80/120 and ascii true/false every line satisfies visibleWidth(line) <= width and lines.length <= rows; the footer 'Topology incomplete unless native relationships are explicitly supplied.' remains.
   Quote: docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-029: "Over 1000 nodes: render cost scales with visible slice and changed ancestors; no full historical-log fold per frame."

B7. Closing the view (Esc from overview) still yields action 'close' with zero producer or control calls (existing WorkflowDialog test keeps passing).
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Navigation": "Closing view never stops workflow."

title: VC-4/W13: Furnace observer projects Attempt nodes, Run->Attempt ownership edges and source intervals (additive)
description:
Gap: nothing in src/ calls ObservationProjection.relate(), so the W15 inspector's graph/overview/timeline never receive a real native edge; FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot() (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts) emits a single Run node and flattens Attempt IDs into evidenceRefs with no Run->Attempt edge and no attempt interval, although FurnaceReading already carries attempts.items[{id,runId,workId,state,outcome,startedAt,finishedAt}] and the native attempts request ID.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): add FurnaceObserver.projectionTopology(reading) returning the unchanged Run snapshot plus one NativeSnapshot per returned Attempt (type 'attempt', bounded intervals from native started_at/finished_at only) and one 'ownership' relation Run->Attempt whose provenance.source is 'furnace' and whose nativeConfirmationRef is the attempts page requestId (the producer's own page asserts attempt.run_id === run.run_id). Partial pages produce no edges for the missing tail; stale readings throw like projectionSnapshot. projectionSnapshot() stays byte-for-byte compatible because src/index.ts:2560 (hot) consumes it; wiring projectionTopology into the Pi observe tool is a separate Sr. Engineer follow-up and is NOT part of this bead.

Files: src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts; test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts (or new test/workbench-furnace-topology.test.ts). Reuse the existing client() mock fixture style. Specs: docs/workbench/09 (Relationships are typed and provenanced; Acceptance/negative controls), docs/workbench/15 VC-4, docs/workbench/02 WB-025/WB-037, docs/workbench/10 Four views (Timeline).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first tests in test/workbench-furnace-observer.test.ts (extend; never delete existing cases) or a new test/workbench-furnace-topology.test.ts, then minimal implementation in src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts ONLY. Hot files (src/index.ts, src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts, ...) must not be touched; keep projectionSnapshot() signature and behavior unchanged because src/index.ts:2560 consumes it.

A1. New additive method FurnaceObserver.projectionTopology(reading: FurnaceReading): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: FurnaceObservedRelation[] } where FurnaceObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate. snapshots[0] deep-equals projectionSnapshot(reading); then one NativeSnapshot per reading.attempts.items entry with source {provider:'furnace', type:'attempt', id:item.id, scope:reading.source.workspaceRoot}, kind 'furnace.attempt.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText item.state (and outcome when present), trace {invocationId: <same as run>, correlationIds:{runId,workId}}, interval ONLY when item.startedAt exists and endedAt ONLY when item.finishedAt exists. No Work node is invented (no Work DTO is read); workId is a correlation id only.
   Quote: docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-025 "Workbench distinguishes Run/Work/Attempt, Forge operation and workspace basis, Claude session, HX coverage, RF provenance."

A2. Exactly one relation per returned attempt: {from: run ref, to: attempt ref, kind:'ownership', provenance:{source:'furnace', observedAt: reading.observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: reading.source.requestIds.attempts}}. No 'dependency', 'causation' or 'hypothesis' edge is ever emitted by this method (test asserts every relation.kind === 'ownership').
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)" and "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source". Quote: docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-4: "Derived tree/timeline shows observed rather than invented edges."

A3. Partial pages: when reading.attempts.complete === false or attempts.unreadableCount > 0, relations exist only for returned items and the Run snapshot coverage stays 'partial'; nothing is synthesized for the missing tail.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 5: "Simulated missing relation; no fabricated dependency edge or precise critical path."

A4. Stale/disconnected reading (freshness !== 'current' or connection !== 'connected') throws CapabilityError category 'unavailable' exactly as projectionSnapshot does; no partial topology is returned.
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Experimental projection implementation": "stale readings cannot refresh confirmed projection state."

A5. Integration proof against the real read model: apply snapshots via projection.refresh and relations via projection.relate on a real ObservationProjection; then projection.query({scope, parent: runRef, limit: 10}) returns exactly the attempt nodes; layoutInspector(...,{view:'graph'}) output contains 'ownership' and '[furnace]'; the timeline view prints a source interval for an attempt with startedAt+finishedAt and 'timing unavailable' for an attempt lacking started_at.
   Quote: docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md section "Four views" Timeline: "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps."

A6. Observer close still invokes zero control verbs (existing assertion pattern: stop/pause/resume/retry mocks have no calls) and no raw log line or redacted secret appears in any snapshot or relation (JSON.stringify(...) does not contain 'TOPSECRET').
   Quote: docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Acceptance/negative controls" item 8: "Closing observer causes zero cancellation calls."

title: defect(wb-g1g.2): topology slice silently undercounts remainder and labels trace observed when projection maxQuery (prod 40) is below requested relationPage (default 100)
description:
Found by flywheel adversarial review run g1-r3 of branch machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.2 (commit 54e4dcc, gate receipt cmd_87383785df8f, which carried this as finding topology-slice-silent-page-cap-undercount, CONFIRMED medium, ownerRulingNeeded).

Defect: selectLinkedTopology silently undercounts the remainder and mislabels the trace "observed" whenever the projection's own relation-page cap (ObservationLimits.maxQuery) is below the selector's requested relationPage (default 100).

Mechanism (verified in code at 54e4dcc): src/workbench/observation.ts:624-625 relations() clamps limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery) and reports no truncation; src/workbench/topology-slice.ts readSide() computes full = rows.length >= page against the REQUESTED page, so a page clamped below the request is indistinguishable from a complete read. The only guard is a doc comment on TopologyCaps.relationPage ("Must not exceed the projection's own page cap") — nothing enforces it, and the DEFAULT (100) violates it for the production projection, which is constructed with maxQuery 40 (wb-6ze.27 description, measured at 24e6015: src/index.ts:2380; W21 bench qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36 also pins 40).

Independent runtime reproduction (review worktree at 54e4dcc, real ObservationProjection, vitest): new ObservationProjection({maxQuery: 40}); 45 observed dependency edges F->n00..n44; selectLinkedTopology default caps returned downstream 10 listed, remainder {count: 30, atLeast: false}, trace {label: "observed", reasons: []}. Truth: 45 observed matching edges, so the true remainder is 35 — 5 observed edges silently dropped, the count claimed exact, and completeness claimed. Control: caps {relationPage: 40} correctly returns remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace with reasons ["relations-truncated"]. This corroborates the gate seat's probe (10 listed + remainder 30 atLeast false, trace observed, 40 of 45).

Why this refutes wb-g1g.2 acceptance: B3 "neighbors beyond caps collapse to a counted remainder, never silently dropped" and the bead title's "missing relations never fabricated, incomplete-trace labeled". A trace labeled "observed" with an exact-claimed remainder while observed matching edges are dropped is a fabricated completeness claim, reachable through the intended consumer path (wb-6ze.24 computes the slice from ObservationProjection typed relations; production maxQuery is 40).

Suggested fix (red-first): falsifier first — maxQuery-40 projection with 45 matching edges under DEFAULT caps must yield remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace/relations-truncated (or an exact count of 35). Then either (a) adopt relationsPage {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} once wb-6ze.27 lands (consumer adoption is explicitly excluded from wb-6ze.27's scope, so no other bead covers this) and treat truncated || limitApplied < requested as a full page, or (b) require/accept the projection's effective page cap from the caller and clamp the requested page to it. Existing behavior when the page is honored (rows.length >= page => atLeast + relations-truncated) is correct and must not regress; never weaken the delivered tests.

title: W14/VC-5: ObservationProjection reports relation-page truncation (new relationsPage returns {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} beside a byte-identical relations(); truncated only when a further MATCHING edge exists past the page, never from index size; cross-scope keys stay empty with examined 0; read-only, no revision change; mirrors the query()/events() shapes); consumer adoption and hot files excluded
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T10:40Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 24e6015, blobless clone, line anchors from `git show HEAD:<path>`): src/workbench/observation.ts:624 `relations(input: {scope; from?; to?; limit?}): Relation[]` clamps `limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? this.limits.maxQuery, this.limits.maxQuery)`, walks the outgoing/incoming/edgesByScope index and `break`s at the limit WITHOUT reporting it, while the sibling reads do report: `query()` (:704) returns `{nodes, examined, truncated}` and `events()` (:767) returns `{events, truncated, completeness}`. Production constructs the projection with maxQuery 40 (src/index.ts:2380, hot, not touched) and the W21 bench-only limits also pin maxQuery 40 (qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36), while consumers request up to 100 (attention.ts:73 RELATION_PAGE = 100; workflow-inspector.ts:92-93 limit:100) or 40 (timeline.ts relationLimit default). Every consumer therefore guesses: attention.ts:141 "relations() reports no truncation and the projection caps each page at its own maxQuery, which this selector cannot see" and re-reads pair by pair under a 2,000-read budget (:75, :155-166); timeline.ts:44 "relations() reports no truncation, so a page capped below this limit cannot be told from a complete one" and :363 flags `truncated.relations` only when `incoming.length >= relationLimit`; workflow-inspector.ts:94-98 "a projection configured below 100 truncates silently, which relations() cannot report". Gate record: the wb-6ze.1 gate accepted "production maxQuery 40 < 100 makes relation-page truncation undetectable through relations(), so (partial) and relations partial fire only at 100"; the wb-6ze.6 gate relayed worker follow-up (3) "relations() reports no truncation, so a reader page cap below relationLimit cannot be detected". The Sr. Engineer approved this bead: BOUNDARY.md 2026-10-15T10:23:58Z "Approved for groom: ... relations() truncation-visibility bead" and 10:32:20Z "the four worker follow-ups are groom-approved".

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observation.ts plus ONE new test file.

- `export interface RelationPage { relations: Relation[]; examined: number; truncated: boolean; limitApplied: number }` and `relationsPage(input: {scope: ObservationScope; from?: string; to?: string; limit?: number}): RelationPage` on ObservationProjection. Same index selection as relations() (outgoing for `from`, incoming for `to`, edgesByScope otherwise), same scope-prefix guard, same exact from/to filters, same `Invalid relation query limit.` throw. `limitApplied = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery)`. `examined` counts edges visited. `truncated` is true iff at least one further MATCHING edge exists beyond the returned rows: the walk looks one matching edge past the limit and stops. It never derives truncation from an index bucket's size, because a bucket may hold edges the exact from/to filter excludes.
- `relations()` keeps its signature and return type; it shares the private walk so `relations(input)` deep-equals `relationsPage(input).relations` for every input (falsifier below).
- Cross-scope `from`/`to` keys (prefix mismatch) return `{relations: [], examined: 0, truncated: false, limitApplied}` exactly as relations() returns `[]` today; a cross-scope caller learns nothing about edge counts.
- Read-only: `revision`, `topologyRevision`, indexes, edges and `stats()` are unchanged by any number of calls; no retained state is added.
- Export RelationPage so attention.ts, timeline.ts, the topology slice and the inspector can adopt it in follow-ups (a sibling adoption bead for attention.ts + timeline.ts is filed blocked-by this bead in the same groom round).

Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (additive method + exported type), test/workbench-observation-relations-page.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation.test.ts may gain additive cases; its existing cases stay untouched.

title: VC-1/W02-C: constant ~2.0 s abort-to-ack in the cancellation path — locate the fixed interval and rule whether it is intended
notes:
[filed by flywheel 2026-10-15 at Sr. Engineer direction, from the wb-a2g.5 closure] Measured on the refined wb-a2g.1 tier at 07faeb3: abort-request-to-acknowledged-cancellation was ~2002-2003 ms in all three counted runs (cmd_27e552e0e099 2002.34, cmd_9b437c8cdf82 2003.27, cmd_4f95a4c061b7 2002.50) and 2001.88 ms in the uncounted pre-commit run — constant to within ~1.5 ms while late-init latencies varied 3-39 ms. That constancy suggests a fixed poll interval or timer in the cancellation ack path, not network variance. Scope: locate the interval (runtime or host), state whether the ~2 s is intended, and if it is a poll, say what a tighter bound costs. Investigation/measurement bead; src changes only if the owner rules the interval a defect. Read BOUNDARY.md at task start.

[flywheel 2026-10-15 ~11:00Z, owner scope ruling] Measurement-only stands UNLESS the finding shows the ~2 s abort-to-ack interval is a Workbench-side wait (ours to fix) rather than SDK wind-down. If Workbench-side, stop at the finding and report; the fix becomes its own bead after the owner rules.

comments.author: flywheel
comments.text: FINDING (ws-03, branch machine/flywheel/wb-a2g.7): the ~2.0 s is SDK-owned, NOT a Workbench wait. Abort -> SDK ProcessTransport.close() ends the child's stdin, then setTimeout(bqe=2000 ms) SIGTERMs a child still alive (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.300 sdk.mjs; unref'd timer, SIGKILL +5 s). The query stream and so host onSettled end when the child's stdout closes; the native claude child does not leave on stdin EOF mid-turn, so ack = 2000 ms + SIGTERM-to-exit (~2-3 ms) = the live 2002-2003 ms. Reproduced through the real createClaudeWorkflowHost: child ignoring EOF acks at ~2008 ms; child exiting on EOF at ~5 ms (same host code). Workbench-side code adds no wait (claude-host.ts has no timer). Tighter bound option: pass spawnClaudeCodeProcess to SIGTERM on abort; cost = bypasses the SDK's graceful stdin-EOF window and its process tracking (risk: truncated session transcript / resume lookup, orphan children on host exit), unmeasured live. Per ruling: stop at finding; no src change. Test pins the behaviour (test/workbench-claude-abort-ack-grace.test.ts); it will go red if an SDK upgrade changes the grace.

Measured: src/workbench/capability-registry.ts CapabilityLimits carries only maxBytes, maxDepth and deadlineMs (lines 58-65, validated at 197-203); invoke() (line 253) applies the deadline timer and the caller signal and nothing else; the only concurrency-adjacent bound anywhere is src/workflow/runtime.ts:690 `const nodeCap = 1000`, a TOTAL node-call count per workflow, so a script's parallel() over hundreds of node() calls dispatches every call at once against the native providers (forge/furnace/hx/rf CLIs and SDK clients) with no admission and no quota. Store dedupe (bd list --status all, terms in-flight/inflight/admission/quota/concurren/backpressure): no bead covers it.

Scope (atomic): src/workbench/capability-registry.ts plus one new test file. One registry-wide bound, no per-capability table (the owner can add one later); no edits to src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/worker-source.ts or src/index.ts (runtime/index.ts are HOT; the worker needs nothing because admission lives host-side where every node(), curated Claude MCP tool and Pi tool path already calls registry.invoke/inspect).

Design to implement:
- CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight?: number, validated exactly like the existing limits (safe integer >= 1, else CapabilityError("validation", "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight.")).
- One exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT (proposed 32) as the default; tests read the constant, never a literal (wb-oon/wb-cax.8 single-carrier precedent).
- Admission applies to invoke mode and inspect mode alike. When inFlight >= maxInFlight the call WAITS in FIFO order for a slot; the wait is bounded by the SAME deadlineMs timer and the SAME caller signal the call already has (no second clock, no new option).
- A call still queued when its deadline fires is refused with CapabilityError("unavailable", ...) whose message names admission and the bound (e.g. "Capability <id> admission exhausted: <maxInFlight> in flight after <deadlineMs>ms."); this is deliberately distinct from the existing CapabilityError("transport", "... exceeded its deadline ...") that means the provider WAS called. A call cancelled while queued keeps the existing "transport" cancellation family. In both cases provider.invoke/inspect is never called for that request.
- A slot is held until the provider promise settles, not until the caller is answered: a hung provider stays counted in inFlight after its caller's deadline rejection, so saturation is visible rather than hidden (honest backpressure; docs/06: a deadline "does not establish producer rollback").
- No automatic retry of a refused or queued-then-cancelled call (docs/06 "No generic auto-retry").
- registry.admission(): Readonly<{maxInFlight; inFlight; peakInFlight; admitted; refused; cancelledWhileQueued}> as a frozen counts-only snapshot for wb-cax.13's "provider call outcomes" telemetry; no ids, no provider names, no payloads.

Red-first: test/workbench-registry-admission.test.ts fails before CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight exists. Base 4ca6bd5 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1. Bound exists and is validated. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution": "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." -> new CapabilityRegistry({maxInFlight: 0}), ({maxInFlight: 1.5}) and ({maxInFlight: -1}) throw CapabilityError category "validation" with message "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight." (the existing limit-validation path); a registry constructed without the option uses the exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT and registry.admission().maxInFlight equals that constant (the test imports the constant; no literal).

A2. FIFO wait, not refusal, while a slot will free. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements": "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." -> with {maxInFlight: 1} and a provider whose invoke resolves only when the test releases it, three concurrent invoke() calls reach provider.invoke one at a time in request order (release #1 -> #2 enters; release #2 -> #3 enters); provider.invoke call count is exactly 1 until the first release; all three callers resolve with their validated values; admission() reports inFlight 0, peakInFlight 1, admitted 3, refused 0 afterwards.

A3. Typed admission refusal, distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md section "Workbench core types" (NodeCallResult): `{ kind: "rejected"; category: "validation" | "authorization" | "unavailable"; diagnostic: string }` and docs/workbench/06 section "Current experimental policy surface": "A deadline stops the caller's wait; it does not establish producer rollback." -> with {maxInFlight: 1, deadlineMs: 50} and the first call held open, a second invoke() rejects with CapabilityError category "unavailable" whose message contains "admission" and the bound; the provider was called exactly once (never for the second request); the message differs from the existing transport-deadline text ("exceeded its deadline"); a third call issued after the first is released succeeds (the refusal left no stale queue state).

A4. Cancellation while queued. docs/workbench/06 section "InvocationContext": "cancellation signal for current wait" -> a queued call whose context.signal aborts rejects with CapabilityError category "transport" (the existing cancellation family), provider.invoke count unchanged, and admission().cancelledWhileQueued increments by one; the slot order of the remaining waiters is unchanged (the next waiter still enters when the running call settles).

A5. Slot held until the provider settles. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "State/event semantics" (via the registry's own deadline comment): a caller rejected by its transport deadline while the provider promise is still pending leaves admission().inFlight at 1 until the provider promise settles; a new call with {maxInFlight: 1} during that window is admission-refused (A3 path) rather than dispatched alongside the hung provider; after the provider settles inFlight returns to 0. Uncertain-effect semantics of the existing deadline path are unchanged (no new "uncertain-effect" category minted here).

A6. Inspect mode shares the bound. docs/workbench/06 section "Optional inspect/observe" -> registry inspect-mode calls occupy the same slots as invoke-mode calls (one held inspect blocks a second invoke under {maxInFlight: 1} and vice versa), proven both directions.

A7. Never auto-retry. docs/workbench/06 section "Registration and resolution": "No generic auto-retry; producer-specific adapters alone may reconcile native logical identities." -> after an admission refusal or a queued cancellation the provider is never invoked later for that request (count asserted after all other calls settle and after one macrotask turn).

A8. Telemetry snapshot is counts only. docs/workbench/17 section "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: ... provider call outcomes ..." and "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." -> admission() returns an Object.isFrozen snapshot with exactly the keys maxInFlight, inFlight, peakInFlight, admitted, refused, cancelledWhileQueued, all safe integers; serialized it contains no capability id, provider name, input or output text (asserted against a fixture whose capability id and payload carry a unique marker).

A9. No production behaviour change elsewhere: src diff touches only src/workbench/capability-registry.ts; all existing registry/security/node-contract/curated-tool suites pass unchanged; biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no hot file touched.

- export interface BeadsReadClient { show(id: string, call: { cwd: string; timeoutMs: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<{ exit: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }> } - injected; tests use a fake; the module never imports node:child_process (static source assertion in the test, like the wb-6ze.10 "SDK never imported" falsifier). BeadsWorkReading = { contract; source: { provider: 'beads'; workId; workspaceRoot; ownership: 'external'; producer: 'bd'; producerVersion?: string (only when the seam measured it, never guessed) }; capturedAt; observedAt; freshness: 'current'; completeness: 'complete' | 'partial'; work: { status: string; issueType: string; priority: number; parent?: string; closedAt?: string; closeReasonPresent: boolean }; dependencies: { offered: number; returned: number; truncated: boolean; items: { id: string; dependencyType: string; status: string }[] }; unmappedDependencyTypes: Record<string, number> }.
  - Identity: the seam runs with cwd = workspaceRoot; options.scope.workspace must equal workspaceRoot (host-bound) else CapabilityError('authorization'). A non-zero exit, non-JSON stdout, a non-array or empty array, or a first element whose id differs from workId is CapabilityError('unavailable') - a missing store or a foreign record is refused, never an empty or borrowed readiness. An aborted signal is CapabilityError('transport').

  - snapshot.source = { provider: 'beads', type: 'work', id: workId, scope: workspaceRoot }; kind 'beads.work.snapshot'; coverage from completeness; node.type 'group' when issueType is 'epic' else 'sdk-operation'; statusText is the native status string verbatim; statusTone: in_progress -> 'active'; open, blocked, deferred -> 'waiting'; closed -> 'unknown' (closure is a readiness fact, not a verified outcome: wb-6ze.12 is closed as a withdrawn duplicate); any unrecognized status -> 'unknown'. No evidenceRefs are invented.
  - relations: each dependencies[] entry with dependency_type 'blocks' -> { kind: 'dependency', from: the work ref, to: { provider: 'beads', type: 'work', id: entry.id, scope: workspaceRoot }, provenance: { source: 'beads', observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: 'bd:show:<workId>' } } - from the dependent work to its blocker, the direction src/workbench/attention.ts:170 already reads dependency edges in; a 'parent-child' entry or the parent field -> ONE { kind: 'grouping', from: parent ref, to: work ref } edge (deduplicated when both name the same id); every other dependency_type -> counted in unmappedDependencyTypes and produces no edge (a native non-dependency link is never minted as a hypothesis or dependency). Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/telemetry.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-telemetry.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const TELEMETRY_CONTRACT = "workbench.telemetry/v1"; export const TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT (event lag compares producer sourceTimestamp with observedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled).
- export type TelemetryMetric<T> = { state: "measured"; value: T; source: "projection" | "supplied" } | { state: "unknown"; reason: "not-supplied" | "invalid-supplied" | "no-source-timestamps" | "no-events" }.
- export interface SuppliedCounters { providerCallOutcomes?: Readonly<Partial<Record<"returned" | CapabilityErrorCategory, number>>>; droppedObservations?: number; lateObservations?: number; visibleRows?: number; renderP95Ms?: number; heapUsedBytes?: number; sdkTokens?: number; claudeSessions?: number; uncertainEffects?: number } -- the host/dialog counts these (ingest results, provider outcomes, render timings, SDK usage) and passes them in; this bead defines the shape only.
- export function buildOperationsTelemetry(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "events" | "stats">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId?: string; now: string; limit?: number (default 100, max 100); eventLimit?: number (default 200, max 1000); supplied?: SuppliedCounters }): OperationsTelemetry -- a frozen report { contract; now; examined: { nodes; truncated; events; eventsTruncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap" }; activeWorkflows: TelemetryMetric<{ active: number; lastKnownRunningStale: number }>; claudeSdkSessions: TelemetryMetric<number> (projection count of nodes with nativeRef.provider "claude-agent-sdk" and type "session"; a supplied claudeSessions is reported beside it with source "supplied", never merged); providerCallOutcomes: TelemetryMetric<Record<string, number>>; eventLag: TelemetryMetric<{ p50Ms; p95Ms; samples; unmeasured; providers: string[]; caveat: string }>; droppedObservations, lateObservations: TelemetryMetric<number>; projectionSize: TelemetryMetric<{ nodes; events; edges }>; visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens, uncertainEffects: TelemetryMetric<number>; nativeEvidenceCoverage: TelemetryMetric<{ withEvidence: number; examined: number }> }.
- Rules: projection-derived metrics come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) page and ONE bounded projection.events({scope, limit: eventLimit}) read; truncated and partial-gap flags are propagated into examined. activeWorkflows.active counts nodes with kind "workflow" and statusTone "active"; lastKnownRunningStale counts those with freshness !== "current" or sourceConnectionState "disconnected" (docs/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity" nuance). eventLag samples are observedAt minus sourceTimestamp in ms for events carrying both (negative samples clamp to 0 and are counted in unmeasured, as are events without sourceTimestamp); p50/p95 by nearest-rank over the sorted samples; providers = sorted distinct event.source.provider. Supplied metrics are measured only when the supplied value is a finite non-negative number (for the outcome record: every value finite non-negative), else unknown "not-supplied" / "invalid-supplied"; the report never defaults an absent counter to 0. now is the caller's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now); the projection is never mutated.
- Redaction: the report contains no node titles, status text, evidence ref strings, prompts, tool bodies or payload refs -- counts and provider names only; provider names pass redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and are capped at 64 chars; JSON.stringify(report) stays under 8 KiB for the maximum page and the test asserts it.

Out of scope: host-side counting (ingest-result counters, provider outcome counters, render timings, SDK usage aggregation live in src/index.ts, the dialog and hosts -- HOT or owner wiring; this bead defines SuppliedCounters only), inspector header or workflow_observe surfacing (wb-752.2), process.memoryUsage or any node:* read inside the module, docs or TRACEABILITY edits.

- Layer 1: a loader is constructed only when input.grants() (read once at construction) contains the row's requiredGrant as an exact string AND the matching reader is supplied; malformed or unknown grant entries are ignored (deny). - Routing: loader.provider equals the row provider; canLoad(ref) is the row's shape check only (uuid shape for claude-message, validated operation id for forge-operation, the furnace reader's own Attempt-id predicate); load(request) throws CapabilityError("validation") when request.nativeRef.provider !== loader.provider or !canLoad(request.evidenceRef) -- the store routes provider-first, the loader never guesses.

• export const CLAUDE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.claude-evidence/v1'; export const CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_GRANT = 'claude:transcript' (the exact literal src/index.ts:4404 checks; docs/20 ruling 6 forbids the two paths diverging).
• export interface ClaudeEvidenceRequest { readTranscript: (sessionId: string, cwd: string, limit: number) => Promise<readonly ClaudeTranscriptRow[]>; grants: () => readonly string[] (the LIVE grant set, re-read on every call); owningSessionNode: { nativeRef: NativeRef; evidenceRefs: readonly string[] } (the projection node the ref was listed on); sessionId: string; cwd: string; evidenceRef: string; windowLimit: number (1..100, the bounded window readClaudeTranscript accepts); maxBytes: number (1..65536); maxLines: number (1..200); timeoutMs: number (1..2147483647); signal: AbortSignal; capturedAt: () => string (injected clock; the module never calls Date.now) }.
• export interface ClaudeEvidenceContent { contract: typeof CLAUDE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT; kind: 'claude.transcript.message'; provider: 'claude-agent-sdk'; nativeRef: NativeRef ({provider:'claude-agent-sdk', type:'message', id: uuid, scope: sessionId}); role: 'user'|'assistant'|'system' (the row type); capturedAt; bytes: number (UTF-8 byte length of the selected row's text as returned by the reader); truncated: boolean (bytes > maxBytes or more than maxLines lines); preview: readonly string[] (the selected row's text split on newlines, each line through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText then a local zero-width strip of U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, max 200 characters, at most maxLines lines, plus a final '… truncated (budget)' line whenever truncated); producerReceipt: { sessionId: string; windowLimit: number; returned: number (rows the reader returned); rowIndex: number (position of the selected row in that window) }; freshness: 'current' } — the docs/20 EvidenceContent shape minus store-level fields, so the claude EvidenceLoader of the wb-g1g.1 follow-up returns it after applying the owning node's freshness.
• export async function readClaudeMessageEvidence(request: ClaudeEvidenceRequest): Promise<ClaudeEvidenceContent> — preconditions before any read (each a CapabilityError, reader never called): grants() not an array, containing non-string entries or any wildcard entry (claude:*, *) -> 'authorization' ("unknown permission data"); missing the exact literal 'claude:transcript' (case-sensitive; 'claude:Transcript', 'transcript', 'claude:*' do not count) -> 'authorization' ("claude:transcript grant required"); owningSessionNode.nativeRef.provider !== 'claude-agent-sdk' || type !== 'session' || id !== sessionId -> 'authorization' ("evidence ref is not listed on a Claude session node of this scope"; a pre-init {provider:'pi-workflow', type:'agent-call'} node, index.ts:2683, is refused because it carries no native session identity); evidenceRef absent from owningSessionNode.evidenceRefs -> 'authorization' (a message of another session is unauthorized); evidenceRef not matching /^claude-message:([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,119})$/ -> 'validation'; windowLimit, maxBytes, maxLines or timeoutMs out of range, or sessionId/cwd empty -> 'validation'; signal already aborted -> 'transport' ("Claude evidence read cancelled before launch"). Exactly one readTranscript(sessionId, cwd, windowLimit) call, raced against request.signal and timeoutMs (abort -> 'transport'; timeout -> 'transport' naming the budget; the reader promise is abandoned, never awaited further). Row validation: every returned row must be an object with type in user|assistant|system, string uuid and string text, else 'unavailable' ("malformed transcript row shape"). Selection: the first row whose uuid === the requested uuid; none inside the returned window -> CapabilityError('transport', "message <uuid> is outside the bounded transcript window (<returned> of limit <windowLimit>)") — never a synthesized row, never a neighbouring row. A thrown reader error is rethrown as CapabilityError('unavailable', preview) where preview is the message through redactWorkbenchText capped at 200 characters, never verbatim. The content never retains the window: no field named rows, lines, message, messages, raw, data or payload, and no other row's text appears anywhere in JSON.stringify(content).
• The module imports only ./claude-transcript.js (type ClaudeTranscriptRow), ./observation.js (type NativeRef), ./capability-registry.js (CapabilityError) and ./redaction.js (redactWorkbenchText, stripUnsafeText) and contains none of 'node:', '@anthropic-ai', 'process.', 'Date.now', 'Math.random', 'import('.

title: W14/VC-5-C: pure attention and bottleneck selector over ObservationProjection (waiting/stale/unknown/disconnected counts, top measured open intervals from source intervals, dependency-chain critical path only as partial-estimated else incomplete-trace with reasons; caller clock, bounded, sanitized); inspector and tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Overview) requires "status and counts, compact nested tree, active operations, attention panel and top measured bottlenecks" with the critical path "shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete", and docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling" requires measured-vs-estimated separation with "incomplete trace" whenever intervals or dependencies are missing. Today src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:156-157 prints two CONSTANT strings regardless of data ('Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress.' and 'Critical path: incomplete trace (no complete dependency/interval proof).'), pinned by test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:112-116 and :195-198. Nothing in src/ computes attention items, bottlenecks or a dependency-chain estimate from observed data: grep -rn 'bottleneck\|criticalPath' src returns only designer.ts:183/236 (criticalPath "unestablished" for run comparisons; hot, untouched) and the inspector constants. wb-6ze.2 (ancestor aggregates in observation.ts) pins criticalPath 'unestablished' and lists "concurrency/critical-path profiling" out of scope; wb-6ze.1 owns the inspector file this run; wb-752.2 builds the workflow_observe reply. This bead supplies the pure selector both consumers wire later.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/attention.ts exporting
• ATTENTION_CONTRACT = "workbench.attention/v1".
• selectAttention(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "relations">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; now: string; limit?: number; bottlenecks?: number }): AttentionReport.
• AttentionReport = { contract: typeof ATTENTION_CONTRACT; basis: "observed"; now: string; examined: { nodes: number; truncated: boolean }; counts: { active; waiting; success; failure; unknown; stale; disconnected; withInterval; withoutInterval }; disconnectedProviders: string[]; bottlenecks: { key; nativeRef; title; tone; freshness; openMs: number; measured: true }[]; unmeasured: number; clockSkew: number; criticalPath: { label: "incomplete-trace"; reasons: ("no-dependency-edges" | "missing-intervals" | "open-intervals" | "hypothesis-edges" | "cycle" | "truncated")[] } | { label: "partial-estimated"; keys: string[]; measuredMs: number; coverage: { chainNodes: number; dependencyEdges: number }; caveat: string }; clockCaveat: string }.
• Rules. `now` is the CALLER's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now()). Nodes come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit: input.limit ?? 100}) call; examined.truncated propagates its truncated flag. openMs = now − interval.startedAt for nodes with statusTone 'active' or 'waiting' that have interval.startedAt and no endedAt; a producer startedAt later than now clamps openMs to 0 and increments clockSkew; nodes without an interval are counted in unmeasured and never ranked; ranking is openMs descending then key ascending (deterministic); bottlenecks.length <= input.bottlenecks ?? 5 and every entry carries measured: true. counts.stale = nodes with freshness !== 'current'; counts.disconnected = nodes with sourceConnectionState 'disconnected'; disconnectedProviders = sorted distinct nativeRef.provider of those nodes. Tones are counted separately (waiting is never folded into active or stale).
• criticalPath. Dependency edges come from projection.relations({scope, from: key, limit}) for examined keys only, kind 'dependency' only. 'partial-estimated' requires ALL of: at least one dependency edge among examined nodes; no 'hypothesis' edge among examined nodes; no cycle on dependency edges; query not truncated; every node on the chosen chain has a COMPLETE interval (startedAt and endedAt). measuredMs is the sum of complete interval durations along the longest-duration dependency chain (DAG longest path); keys lists that chain in dependency order; the caveat literal is "Observed dependency edges and complete source intervals only; missing edges do not imply independence." Anything else returns incomplete-trace carrying EVERY applicable reason. The label is never "exact" or "complete" and no number is emitted without the partial-estimated label.
• clockCaveat literal: "openMs uses the caller clock against producer startedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled."
• Every title passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts; do not edit) and is cut to 120 characters; control characters never survive; JSON.stringify(report).length < 16384 at limit 100 / bottlenecks 5.

title: VC-7/W18-B: pure native executable identity observation (realpath + sha256 for absolute paths, PATH-resolved binaries labelled mutable-path, SDK default executable labelled unsupported, never executes) plus reattach comparison that never upgrades unknown to same; detached host wiring excluded
description:
Gap: docs/workbench/15 names "native immutable deployment refs" as VC-7 acceptance and docs/workbench/08 says native executable identity is an unestablished release obligation; W18 (wb-5w0) notes "Native binaries ... not claimed" and W22 (wb-cax) notes "Full release/install native binary identity ... remain open". At rig ad3cf6e the detached host hard-codes `nativeRuntimeIdentity: "unsupported"` (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:82 and :96) and its runtimeClosure comment reads "Native executables launched by SDK defaults/PATH still have unsupported identity."; src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 launches ServerConnection.spawn("forge"), a bare PATH-resolved name; the Claude Agent SDK's Options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1984) "Uses the built-in executable if not specified." Nothing in src/ can observe, pin or compare the bytes of a native executable, so no host can honestly report which binary it launched or refuse reattachment when that binary changed.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/executable-identity.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT = 'workbench.executable-identity/v1'
- export type ExecutableIdentityReason = 'sdk-default-executable' | 'not-found' | 'not-a-file' | 'not-executable' | 'symlink-depth' | 'too-large' | 'unreadable' | 'path-resolved' | 'shadowed-candidates' | 'search-truncated' (frozen set; nothing else is ever emitted).
- export interface ExecutableObservation { contractVersion: typeof EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT; requested: string | undefined; resolution: 'absolute' | 'path-search' | 'unresolved'; resolvedPath?: string; realPath?: string; symlinkHops: number; digest?: string (sha256:<hex>); sizeBytes?: number; mode?: number; candidates: number; immutability: 'digest-observed' | 'mutable-path' | 'unsupported'; reasons: readonly ExecutableIdentityReason[]; observedAt: string }
- export function observeExecutableIdentity(input: { command: string | undefined; cwd: string; path: string | undefined; observedAt: string; maxBytes?: number; maxSearchEntries?: number; maxSymlinkHops?: number }): ExecutableObservation — synchronous; reads only through node:fs (lstat, readlink, stat, chunked reads for hashing — never readFileSync of a whole binary); never imports node:child_process; never reads process.env (PATH is an explicit input); never throws for a missing, unreadable, non-regular, non-executable or oversized target — those are 'unresolved'/'unsupported' with a reason.
  • command undefined or empty -> resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] (the honest answer for the Claude built-in executable and any SDK default).
  • command containing a path separator -> resolved against cwd; symlinks followed hop by hop (count hops; above maxSymlinkHops, default 16, -> 'unsupported' with 'symlink-depth'); must be a regular file with an execute bit; hashed with sha256 when sizeBytes <= maxBytes (default 512 MiB) -> resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed'; oversize -> digest omitted, immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['too-large'].
  • bare command -> PATH searched in order (split on path.delimiter; at most maxSearchEntries, default 64, further entries ignored and 'search-truncated' recorded; relative or empty entries resolved against cwd); the first regular executable file wins; candidates counts every searched entry holding a same-named executable; resolution 'path-search'; the digest IS observed but immutability is 'mutable-path' with reasons ['path-resolved'] plus 'shadowed-candidates' when candidates > 1. A digest never upgrades a PATH-resolved binary to 'digest-observed'.
  • Result and its reasons are frozen; resolvedPath and realPath pass through redactWorkbenchText (paths may embed tokens); absent fields mean not observed, never a default.
- export function compareExecutableIdentity(recorded: ExecutableObservation, current: ExecutableObservation): { verdict: 'same' | 'changed' | 'unknown'; differences: readonly string[] } — 'same' only when both digests are present and equal AND both immutability values are 'digest-observed'; 'changed' when both digests are present and differ; otherwise 'unknown' (a mutable-path or unsupported side can never yield 'same'); differences names each differing field (digest, realPath, sizeBytes, mode, immutability, resolution).

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts (in flight under wb-6hb.1; the 'unsupported' literal is W18's later wiring point), src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workbench/identity.ts; discovering the Claude built-in executable path from SDK internals; remote host authentication; Furnace ExecutorApp. If acceptance cannot be met without touching a hot or reserved file, stop and return blocked.

Specs: docs/workbench/08 (Separate four identities; Experimental immutable receipt; Optional local detached profile; Run recovery and journal design), docs/workbench/17 (Versioning / distribution), docs/workbench/12 (Supply chain; Credential boundaries), docs/workbench/15 (Vertical cuts VC-7), docs/workbench/02 WB-014/WB-041.

title: VC-7/W18-A: detached-host fault-injection conformance tier (effect-then-crash before host result, SIGTERM on a running owned host, cancel isolation across two hosts, shutdown unresolvedEffects) with exactly-once effect markers and an evidence-grade receipt; measurement-only, dist imports, src untouched
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0): VC-7 (wb-0kg) names "crash/uncertain-operation conformance" and has no decomposition bead; W18 (wb-5w0) notes claim "unknown no retry afterloss" from qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs (cmd_b21303c30b15), which kills a host DURING a provider wait (SIGKILL) and inspects after a graceful shutdown, proving inspect() -> unknown + reconcileHint, execute() rejection and same-id relaunch conflict. Nothing kills the host AFTER a provider side effect has happened but BEFORE the host records the result (docs/workbench/14 § "Fault-injection locations": "after provider side effect but before host result"); nothing proves the effect happened exactly once and is never repeated through reattach, execute or relaunch; nothing shows that cancelling one host leaves a sibling host running ("no implicit mass cancellation"); and the shutdown reply's unresolvedEffects flag (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts connectDetachedWorkflow().shutdown -> { accepted, unresolvedEffects }) is never asserted. TRACEABILITY WB-026 and WB-041 stay fixture/experimental.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; src/ untouched: src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts is reserved by wb-6hb.1 and only its compiled dist/ output is driven here):
1. qa/workbench/local-detached-faults-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): faultProviderSource({ capabilityId, markerDirectory, crashAfterEffect }) returning the ESM text of a trusted-local provider (effectClass "write", permissions ["fixture:effect"], contractSource "fixture:source") whose invoke(input, ctx) appends one marker file "<markerDirectory>/<ctx.invocationId>.<n>" (the irreversible effect) and, when crashAfterEffect is true, calls process.kill(process.pid, "SIGKILL") synchronously BEFORE returning so the host never records a result; assessFaultJourneys(observed) -> { findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean }; buildFaultReceipt(input) -> frozen { contract: "workbench.detached-faults/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, journeys, markerCounts, findings, realised, pass }.
2. qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs (new runner; imports ../../dist/workbench/hosts/local-detached.js exactly like qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs plus node: builtins; mkdtemp workspace mode 0700 with the provider module, helper and marker directory inside it; every host SIGTERMed and the directory removed in finally):
   F1 effect-then-crash: launch invocation "effect-crash" with the crashing provider (grants ["fixture:effect"], localProvider manifest with the module digest, permissions ["inspect", "execute"]); poll inspect() until terminal "unknown"; then execute() must reject, launchDetachedWorkflow with the same invocationId must reject /exists|conflict/, and the marker count for "effect-crash" must be exactly 1 after all three; then launch "effect-crash-second" (an explicit NEW logical invocation with the same input) and record that it is accepted and writes its own single marker (total 2 across two ids, labelled explicitSecondRequest).
   F2 cancel isolation: launch "iso-a" and "iso-b" with a non-crashing wait provider (ms 10000); cancel "iso-a" with a bounded reason; record accepted/terminalConfirmed; poll "iso-a" to terminal "cancelled"; inspect "iso-b": observation "observed-running" or "observed-started", terminal undefined, cancellationRequested false, controlAudit empty; then shutdown both.
   F3 shutdown with unresolved effects: launch "unresolved" (wait 10000, running) and "idle" (autoStart false, never executed); shutdown both; record unresolvedEffects true for "unresolved" and false for "idle"; inspect "unresolved" afterwards -> terminal "unknown" with reconcileHint, never "completed".
   F4 SIGTERM on an owned running host "sigterm": process.kill(pid, "SIGTERM"); poll inspect() -> terminal "unknown"; execute() rejects; marker count unchanged.
   Each journey records timestamps and the measured latency from kill/cancel to the first unknown/cancelled observation.
3. Exit semantics (receipt printed as one JSON line and written to $DETACHED_FAULTS_RECEIPT when set, BEFORE exiting): 0 = realised and no findings; 1 = realised with findings (a measured violation, recorded honestly); 2 = not realised (non-Linux or setuid operator per localOperator(), missing dist/ build, or the crashing provider did not terminate the host within 5 s) with a diagnostic.

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts or any src/ file (if a journey measures a violation - a replayed effect, a sibling cancelled, a fabricated terminal verdict - record the finding in the ledger line and bead notes and return blocked); remote authentication, other-UID negatives, Furnace ExecutorApp hosting and native binary identity (each needs live hosts or the reserved file); W12 effect-metadata refusal on resume (lands with wb-6hb.1; a follow-up extends this tier to assert the typed uncertain-effect once describeNodeEffect exists); editing qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md.

acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts fails before qa/workbench/local-detached-faults-receipt.mjs exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

D1. An effect that happened is never repeated and never reported as a verdict. In F1 the marker count for "effect-crash" is exactly 1 after the crash, after inspect() reports terminal "unknown" (observation "unknown", source "local-client-transport", reconcileHint matching /never.*retry|do not.*retry/i, no result field), after execute() rejected and after the same-id relaunch rejected /exists|conflict/; the snapshot never reports terminal "completed" or "failed" for that invocation. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Adversarial test matrix": "Kill after Furnace side effect before returned Run ID; kill after workspace edit before recorded result; ... Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Optional local detached profile": "Inspection after host loss reports unknown with producer reconciliation guidance; it does not replay a saved terminal verdict or rerun JavaScript." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-026: "Interrupted effectful operation is reconciled through producer or marked uncertain; no automatic blind repeat."

D2. A lost result is not evidence the effect did not happen. The F1 receipt records effectObserved true (the marker exists) together with terminal "unknown", and the assessor records finding "effect-denied" if any journey field claims the effect did not occur. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "An observed timeout or disconnect is *not* evidence that side effect never happened." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md § "Nonfunctional invariants" NFR-02: "No host auto-retry of ambiguous irreversible writes."

D3. A deliberate second request is a new logical invocation, not a retry. "effect-crash-second" is accepted, writes exactly one marker of its own, and the receipt labels it explicitSecondRequest true with totalMarkers 2 across two ids; a relaunch under the ORIGINAL id stays refused. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Separate four identities": "Logical invocation: caller-created unique identity stable across retry of same request; distinct from identical intentional second request." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "A Pi UI reconnect is only an observer/client action; it must not restart external work."

D4. Cancellation has three phases and touches one host. In F2 cancel() returns { accepted: true, terminalConfirmed: false }; the next inspect() of "iso-a" shows cancellationRequested true before terminal "cancelled" appears; "iso-b" keeps observation "observed-running" or "observed-started", terminal undefined, cancellationRequested false and controlAudit [] throughout, and ends only by its own shutdown command. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Cancellation and ownership": "Multi-reader shared child MUST NOT be stopped merely because one reader closed Pi or stopped waiting." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Concurrent readers with one shared child; stopping one reader must not stop child without ownership."

D5. Shutdown reports unresolved effects honestly. In F3 shutdown of the running "unresolved" host returns unresolvedEffects true and of the never-executed "idle" host returns unresolvedEffects false; the later inspect() of "unresolved" is terminal "unknown" with a reconcileHint, never "completed". Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "Shutdown: stop accepting calls, notify owned local tasks, attempt graceful end, report unresolved effects, and release owned resources." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-041: "Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability."

D6. SIGTERM is loss, not completion. In F4 inspect() after SIGTERM reaches terminal "unknown" within 5 s (latency recorded), execute() rejects, and the marker count is unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Lifetimes": "Detached service: independent process survives Pi client disconnect but does not guarantee service crash recovery." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "The local detached shell tier is a separate process-lifecycle proof, not remote authentication or native crash-durability evidence."

D7. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts: a journey with marker count 2 under one id -> finding "duplicate-effect"; terminal "completed" after crash -> finding "fabricated-terminal"; same-id relaunch accepted -> finding "reuse-after-loss"; sibling cancellationRequested true or terminal "cancelled" -> finding "mass-cancellation"; unresolvedEffects false for a running host -> finding "unresolved-effects-hidden"; a clean fixture -> pass true with every receipt field present; the generated provider text contains exactly one marker write before process.kill and none after. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." Nothing from node:fs, node:child_process or any provider):
• PATCH_PROPOSAL_CONTRACT = "workbench.patch-proposal/v1"; class PatchProposalError extends Error { code: "SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH" | "CANDIDATE_TOO_LARGE" | "PROMOTION_PRECONDITION" | "VALIDATION" }.
• proposeWorkflowPatch(input: { base: WorkflowSource; candidateSource: string; rationale: string; hypothesis?: { metric: string; direction: "lower" | "higher"; groundedIn: readonly string[] }; pinnedInvocations?: readonly InvocationSnapshot[]; registry?: CapabilityRegistry; grants?: readonly string[]; limits?: { maxDiffLines?: number; maxPreviewBytes?: number } }): WorkflowPatchProposal.
  – First check: base.definition.artifactDigest must equal `sha256:<hex>` of base.source (same form designer.ts uses) else throw PatchProposalError("SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH") before any diff or validation work.
  – candidate.definition = { ...base.definition, artifactDigest: sha256(candidateSource) }; validation = validateWorkflowSource({ definition: candidate.definition, sourceRef: base.sourceRef, source: candidateSource }, { registry, grants }) so SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, control-character, META and possible-call/grant diagnostics are inherited unchanged and `executed` stays false.
  – diff: deterministic line diff (LCS or Myers) over base vs candidate; hunks `{ op: "context" | "add" | "remove"; baseLine?: number; candidateLine?: number; text: string }` with text = safeWorkflowTerminalText(redactWorkbenchText(line)); bounded by limits.maxDiffLines (default 400) and limits.maxPreviewBytes (default 65536) with `truncated: boolean`; `summary: { added, removed, unchanged }` counted over the FULL diff even when the preview is truncated; identical bytes -> status "no-change" with zero hunks.
  – affectedPinnedInvocations: for each pinnedInvocations entry whose scriptDigest === base.definition.artifactDigest -> { logicalInvocationId, scriptDigest, action: "unchanged", note: "remains pinned to the base digest; the candidate requires a new logical invocation" }; other snapshots are only counted in unrelatedInvocations; input snapshots are never mutated.
  – promotion: { state: "proposed"; requires: "operator"; applied: false }; experiment: { independentVariable: "source"; referenceDigest; candidateDigest; mustHold: ["inputDigest", "modelDigest", "toolsDigest", "environmentDigest", "cacheDigest"] } (the CompareRun field names, so compareWorkflowRuns can later treat source as the only intended difference); hypothesis echoed with grounding: "ungrounded" when groundedIn is empty; causalClaim: false; status: validation.status ("valid" | "invalid" | "uncertain") or "no-change"; contractVersion; proposalDigest = identityDigest("patch-proposal", <proposal without proposalDigest>).
  – Every returned object is deep-frozen plain data; JSON round-trip is lossless.
• recordPromotionDecision(proposal, decision: { decision: "promoted" | "rejected" | "deferred"; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; at: string; reason: string }): PromotionReceipt — frozen; "promoted" requires proposal.status === "valid" else throw PatchProposalError("PROMOTION_PRECONDITION"); receipt fields: contractVersion, proposalDigest, decision, principal, at, reason, appliesTo: "versioned-source", appliedByWorkbench: false, pinnedInvocationsChanged: 0. The module exports no function that accepts a filesystem path.

title: W21-A: deterministic nested-group 10k swarm fixture + bounded grouped projection/inspector benchmark receipt (no cap raise)
description:
Build the measurement harness W21 needs BEFORE any node-cap or aggregation decision. The projection (src/workbench/observation.ts store()) FIFO-evicts the oldest node once maxNodes (default 2000) is reached, so a 10k-operation swarm is silently truncated today; this bead measures that honestly rather than hiding it or raising caps.

Deliver three artifacts, nothing else:
1. test/helpers/swarm-fixture.ts — a deterministic (seeded, no Date.now()/Math.random() in the measured path) generator that yields: >=10,000 `sdk-operation` nodes under 5-level nested `group` nodes joined by `grouping` relations; partial `dependency` and `hypothesis` links (not every node linked); long Unicode titles (CJK, combining marks); large payloadRef strings; and a tick stream of 1-100 active status changes per tick totalling >=100,000 ObservationEvents, all under one invocationId and one ObservationScope. Mixed providers (forge/furnace/claude-agent-sdk) with colliding numeric ids to exercise provider-qualified keys.
2. qa/workbench/grouped-bench.mjs (dist/ imports, same shape as qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs) plus a `[build.commands.grouped-bench]` entry in forge.toml: ingest the fixture into `new ObservationProjection()` with DEFAULT limits (maxNodes 2000, maxEdges 4000 — do not raise), then take 1000 keyboard navigation + layoutInspector samples cycling overview/graph/timeline/details at 80x24, 120x40 and ASCII tier, plus resize samples (80x24 <-> 120x40), and write a JSON receipt (W21_BENCH_RECEIPT env path, like W15_BENCH_RECEIPT).
3. test/workbench-grouped-bench.test.ts — vitest guard: two generations of the fixture are deep-equal; group depth is exactly 5; operations >= 10,000; events >= 100,000; ticks have 1..100 changes; the receipt shape has every field named in the acceptance; and a falsifier that fails if the bench projection is constructed with maxNodes > 2000 or maxEdges > 4000.

Out of scope (separate follow-up beads): raising caps, adding ancestor/supernode aggregation to observation.ts or workflow-inspector.ts, dialog wiring, any hot file. Do not modify qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs or test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts.

title: wb-g1g.1 review: evidence preview bounding cuts inside UTF-8 sequences and UTF-16 surrogate pairs (boundPreview/safeChunks), fabricating U+FFFD and lone surrogates and exceeding maxBytes by up to 2 bytes
description:
Adversarial review finding (flywheel reviewer, run g1-r3) against machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.1 @ 96b64fa (tree 9cd29f2, gate cmd_a8b4e1ffdff4). Reproduced in a detached review worktree at 96b64fa with vitest 4.1.10; probe files were deleted after the run, nothing tracked was modified.

CONFIRMED: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts bounds preview text by raw UTF-8 bytes and by UTF-16 code units, never by code points, so the bounded preview can contain characters the evidence never contained and can exceed the per-entry byte budget.

1. boundPreview (evidence-loader.ts, `Buffer.from(part).subarray(0, remaining).toString()`): a byte cut inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence decodes to U+FFFD. Probe: loader preview ['漢'.repeat(1000)] with bytes 3000, store maxBytes 100 -> loaded entry whose preview content (excluding the '[truncated]' marker) is 102 bytes and whose last content line ends in U+FFFD ('漢'x33 + '�'). Measured: {"sum":113,"withoutMark":102,"maxBytes":100,"hasFFFD":true}. The bead's AC3 says "at most maxBytes per entry"; the overshoot is bounded (at most 2 bytes: a 1-byte partial replaced by a 3-byte U+FFFD) but it is a measured violation, and the U+FFFD is a glyph not present in the source.

2. safeChunks (evidence-loader.ts, `cleaned.slice(at, at + EVIDENCE_LINE_CHARS)`): slicing at 240 UTF-16 code units splits a surrogate pair when the boundary is odd relative to the pairs. Probe: preview ['a' + '😀'.repeat(130)] (261 code units) -> two chunks of lengths [240, 21]; chunk 0 ends with "\ude00\ud83d" (an unpaired high surrogate) and chunk 1 starts with "\ude00\ud83d" (an unpaired low surrogate). Measured: {"loneSurrogatePerLine":[true,true]}. Neither redactWorkbenchText, stripUnsafeText (UNSAFE_TEXT covers C0/C1 and bidi only), the loader's zero-width strip nor safeWorkflowTerminalText removes lone surrogates, so they survive into the EvidenceEntry and, in the Unicode tier, into the inspector's `add()`/`safe()` output (the ASCII tier masks them as '?'). The existing suites only exercise ASCII payloads at the byte boundary ('x'.repeat(1 MiB)) and even-length emoji-free lines, so neither case is pinned; the 107 existing cases pass.

Why it matters (quoted criteria from the bead): AC3 docs/workbench/09 "store reference/short redacted preview" -> "at most maxBytes per entry (preview bounded)"; AC4 docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display" and docs/workbench/10 "visible unknowns, never fabricated". A preview that shows U+FFFD or lone surrogates displays text the source never carried; the bounded view should cut on code-point boundaries and keep the byte budget exact.

Suggested fix (evidence-loader.ts only; no hot or do-not-edit file): in boundPreview, accumulate code points (for..of) while Buffer.byteLength(cp) fits `remaining`, never cut inside a sequence; in safeChunks, chunk with Array.from(cleaned) (code points) so a pair is never split; optionally strip any remaining lone surrogate in the loader's own local pass (ruling 8 already gives that pass the zero-width strip). Red-first pins in test/workbench-evidence-loader.test.ts: (a) '漢'.repeat(1000) at maxBytes 100 -> content bytes <= 100 and no U+FFFD in any line; (b) 'a'+'😀'.repeat(130) -> no lone surrogate in any chunk (regex /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/ matches no line); plus one inspector case rendering (b) at 120x40 Unicode tier with the same assertion over every output line, visibleWidth <= width.
