title: claude evidence loader stamps capturedAt from the host clock when no now() is injected
description: Machine finding during wb-g1g.1 verification (evidence-producers.ts:84): the claude session loader falls back to Date.now()/new Date() for capturedAt when deps carry no now(). Workbench convention injects now() at every wiring site (reconcile tool, decision cores) so records are testable and resume-stable. Fix: require now in the loader deps (or thread the one index.ts injects) and drop the fallback; pin with a test that a loader built without a clock refuses rather than invents a timestamp.

title: redactWorkbenchText is not idempotent on a JSON-embedded secret: the second pass eats the closing brace
description: Machine finding during wb-g1g.1 verification: redactWorkbenchText applied twice to a JSON string containing a secret removes the closing brace on the second pass (over-redaction only, never a leak), contrary to the docs/20 ruling-2 wording that redaction is stable. Fix: make the replacement pattern idempotent (match the already-redacted marker) and pin with redact(redact(x)) === redact(x) over the probe corpus.
notes: Scope note from the wb-6ze.8 gate relay: redaction.ts's second pass only swaps matches for markers or truncates, so the non-idempotence is a preview-shape question (an eaten closing brace), never a secret surviving. The fix should also reconcile docs/20 ruling 2's wording, which currently calls double redaction idempotent; either make it true (idempotent replacement that recognizes its own marker) or correct the ruling text to over-redaction-only, in the same commit.

title: W22-L/docs-16: fork divergence record and census falsifier (docs/16 'Record fork divergence in this documentation': a measured table of pre-existing upstream paths the fork modified since the TRACEABILITY baseline, checked by one vitest diffing baseline..HEAD for upstream-owned src/ and test/ paths; unrecorded divergence fails naming the path, a stale row fails, git or baseline unavailable fails explicitly; red at 250c0af with 17 unrecorded paths); docs/16 table + one test, no src edits
description:
Gap (measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program 250c0af, groom seat g2 round 12): docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Upstream maintainability" requires "Record fork divergence in this documentation" and "Keep a focused upstream sync process that checks source changes to runtime, worker, progress, dialog and SDK APIs", and section "Principle" requires "preserve source history/tests/upstream update path". Nothing records or checks the divergence. Measured with `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M 38034a043e63a65ec5a81544c7a81d0e6b76ebe3..origin/workbench/implementation-program -- src ':!src/workbench' test ':!test/workbench*'` (the baseline is the fork sha TRACEABILITY.md names in its "Baseline:" line; `git cat-file -t` confirms it is a reachable commit): 17 pre-existing upstream paths are modified - src/index.ts, src/settings.ts, src/ui/workflow-card.ts, src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts, src/ui/workflow-menu.ts, src/workflow/host.ts, src/workflow/journal.ts, src/workflow/meta.ts, src/workflow/progress.ts, src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/saved.ts, src/workflow/task.ts, src/workflow/tool-description.ts, src/workflow/worker-source.ts, test/workflow-meta.test.ts, test/workflow-progress.test.ts, test/workflow-task.test.ts. The docs/16 section "Source-level refactor plan" table names 12 planned paths; it omits src/settings.ts, src/ui/workflow-menu.ts, src/workflow/meta.ts, src/workflow/saved.ts, src/workflow/task.ts, src/workflow/tool-description.ts and the three tests, and still lists src/agent-runner.ts, src/ui/conversation-viewer.ts and src/ui/fleet-list.ts, which are unmodified. The record is stale in both directions and no falsifier exists (bd census: no bead mentions fork divergence, upstream sync or the baseline census; wb-wh7 W01 recorded the baseline only). Newly added files such as src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts are not divergence of an upstream path and are out of this census by construction (--diff-filter=M).

Scope (atomic, test-only plus one docs table; src/ untouched; hot-file free):
- docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md gains a section "## Measured fork divergence" holding one table with columns path | recorded at (short sha) | note, listing every pre-existing upstream path the fork has modified. The baseline sha is NOT repeated there: the single carrier stays the TRACEABILITY.md "Baseline:" line, which the test parses (wb-cax.8 single-carrier rule).
- test/workbench-upstream-divergence.test.ts (new): reads the baseline sha from docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md, verifies it is a reachable commit (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`), runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M <sha> HEAD -- src ':!src/workbench' test ':!test/workbench*'` via execFileSync('git', [...]) with cwd at the repository root, parses the docs/16 table, and asserts set equality both ways: a divergent path missing from the table fails naming the path and the sentence to add ("record it in docs/workbench/16 section Measured fork divergence"); a table row whose path no longer differs from the baseline fails as stale; a table row whose path never existed at the baseline fails as misrecorded. When git is unavailable, the repository is not a checkout, or the baseline commit is unreachable (shallow clone), the test FAILS with a message beginning "unknown:" and the reason - it never passes and never silently skips (docs/14 "An omitted test level needs an explicit reason; never imply it ran"). No environment variable disables the check.
- Red: the test fails at 250c0af before the table exists, listing all 17 paths. Green: the table records the 17 measured paths at the recording sha. Falsifier proof: temporarily appending an unrecorded path's modification (in the test's own temp git fixture, not the rig) turns the check red; a stale row turns it red.
- To keep the gate hermetic the test uses the real repository for the measurement AND a small temporary git repository fixture (mkdtemp, `git init`, two commits) for the red/stale falsifiers, so the falsifiers do not depend on mutating the rig.

Out of scope: editing any src/ file; modifying the docs/16 "Source-level refactor plan" table (planned paths stay a plan; the new table is the measured record); the TRACEABILITY validator (wb-cax.1); any hot file (BOUNDARY 40a031a entry plus src/ui/workflow-card.ts); qa/ scripts or forge.toml.

Files: docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md (one new section), test/workbench-upstream-divergence.test.ts (new). Specs: docs/workbench/16 (Principle; Upstream maintainability), docs/workbench/14 (Truth labels and release gates), docs/workbench/17 (Release checklist item 1), docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md (Baseline line, single carrier of the fork sha).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-upstream-divergence.test.ts fails at 250c0af before docs/workbench/16 carries the "Measured fork divergence" table, naming all 17 measured paths. Base 250c0af or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

C1. docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md section "Upstream maintainability": "Record fork divergence in this documentation." - the new docs/16 table lists every pre-existing upstream path (src/ and test/ outside src/workbench and test/workbench*) modified since the baseline, and the test asserts the table equals the measurement in both directions (unrecorded path fails naming it; stale row fails; misrecorded path fails).
C2. Same section: "Keep a focused upstream sync process that checks source changes to runtime, worker, progress, dialog and SDK APIs." - the measurement is `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M <baseline> HEAD -- src ':!src/workbench' test ':!test/workbench*'`, so any new edit to an upstream file (runtime, worker, progress, dialog, index, settings, tests) is caught at the candidate's own HEAD until it is recorded.
C3. docs/workbench/16 section "Principle": "Move only enough code to establish correct boundaries; preserve source history/tests/upstream update path." - the census reports modifications only (--diff-filter=M); newly added Workbench files are not counted as upstream divergence, and no src/ file changes in this bead.
C4. docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md "Baseline: fork `38034a043e63a65ec5a81544c7a81d0e6b76ebe3`" is the single carrier of the baseline sha: the test parses it and the docs/16 table does not repeat it (wb-cax.8 single-carrier rule); the test verifies the sha is a reachable commit before measuring.
C5. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md section "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." and TRACEABILITY "Evidence rules": "An omitted test level needs an explicit reason; never imply it ran." - git unavailable, not a checkout, or unreachable baseline FAILS with a message starting "unknown:" and the reason; there is no environment switch that turns the check into a pass.
C6. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Release checklist" item 1: "Sources and upstream license preserved; fork origin recorded." - the recorded table names the recording sha per row so the record is dated evidence, not a claim.
C7. Hermetic falsifier proof: the test builds a temporary git repository fixture (mkdtemp, git init, two commits) to prove the unrecorded-path and stale-row failures without mutating the rig; the proposed closure quotes the red run, the green run and the fixture falsifier run.
